chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il ibn Khirash from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)
Regarding four men who testified against a woman for adultery, one of them being her husband, he said: 'The husband performs li'an (mutual cursing), and the others are flogged.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an when a husband accuses his wife of adultery with three other witnesses?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib clarifies the procedural distinction in li'an where the husband's accusation triggers the mutual cursing ritual, while the other three witnesses, having provided partial testimony, are subject to flogging. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the husband's role is unique in establishing the penalty of exile or divorce through li'an, whereas the others' testimony is treated as standard qadhf. This distinction underscores the precision in applying hudud penalties based on the specific status of the accuser.
